original_question: Does complex projective 3-space CP^3 admit a complex structure whose second Chern class vanishes, equivalently a non-Kahler complex structure whose existence would in particular have consequences for the long-standing question of whether S^6 admits a complex structure?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 13: Does there exist a complex structure on P^3 (= CP^3) with vanishing second Chern class?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct paper target: Section 6's Problem 13 asks about the existence of a complex structure on CP^3 with vanishing second Chern class. You also picked up the two nearby contextual remarks that the paper attaches to this problem: any such structure would have to be non-Kähler, and the question is linked to the still-open problem of whether S^6 admits a complex structure.
missing_details: The paper is asking about the smooth manifold underlying the standard complex projective 3-space CP^3; to make the question stand-alone, that smooth-manifold viewpoint should be stated explicitly.
The question is purely existential: it asks whether there exists at least one such complex structure, not for a classification of non-Kähler complex structures on CP^3.
The relevant Chern class is the second Chern class of the holomorphic tangent bundle of the putative complex manifold, and vanishing means c_2(T^{1,0}_J CP^3)=0 in H^4(CP^3; Z).

In the paper, non-Kählerness is only a necessary consequence of the condition c_2=0; it is not an equivalent replacement for that condition. A bare question about existence of a non-Kähler complex structure on CP^3 would drift toward the broader Problem 28.

The S^6 relation is one-way in the paper: a negative answer to Problem 13 would imply that S^6 has no complex structure; equivalently in context, if S^6 had a complex structure, then blowing up a point would produce a complex structure on CP^3 with c_2=0.
If one wants full paper-faithfulness, 'complex structure' should be understood as an integrable almost complex structure on the standard smooth manifold CP^3.
refined_question: Does the smooth manifold underlying complex projective 3-space CP^3 admit an integrable complex structure J such that the second Chern class of its holomorphic tangent bundle vanishes, i.e. c_2(T^{1,0}_J CP^3)=0 in H^4(CP^3; Z)?
equivalent_formulation: Does the standard smooth manifold CP^3 admit a non-Kähler complex structure J with c_2(T^{1,0}_J CP^3)=0 in H^4(CP^3; Z)?
justification: The draft is trying to capture Section 6, Problem 13, not the broader classification question of Problem 28. Problem 13 is stated exactly as the existence of a complex structure on P^3 with vanishing second Chern class. On the same page, the paper explains the two surrounding facts reflected in your draft: first, such a structure cannot be Kähler, by reference to Problem 28*; second, a negative answer to Problem 13 would imply that S^6 does not admit a complex structure, because a complex structure on S^6 would yield one on P^3 with c_2=0 by blowing up a point. The main correction needed is that 'non-Kähler' is not by itself equivalent to the paper's question; the paper's target remains the sharper c_2=0 existence problem on the standard smooth CP^3.
